scope_lock.source: User request: a barrier-side TV showing the parking map with a path from the ramp head to a suitable destination when Camera AI reports a vehicle, plus updating the Dieu huong xe map to derive per-block coordinates. Confirmed by three user decisions: a separate kiosk view rather than reusing the operator page, a real lane graph with Dijkstra rather than a schematic polyline, and a server-chosen destination block persisted with the routing decision.
in_scope: lane_node, lane_edge, and block.lane_node_id persisted in the plan_map.jpg 1200x1139 routing frame
one is_entry lane node replacing BlockMapRepository.GateX/GateY as the route origin authority
Euclidean-weighted Dijkstra from the is_entry node to a block arrival node
server-side destination block selection inside the ZoneRouter-chosen zone, persisted on vehicle_routing.block_no
GET /Monitor/DriverRoute with states ROUTE, MESSAGE, and WAITING under a 90-second freshness window
a new Home/DriverGuide full-screen view polling that endpoint every 2 seconds
removing the client-side block-candidate selection from Views/Home/Routing.cshtml
registering the new view in TotalParking.csproj and the _ScadaLayout sidebar active-state expression
out_of_scope: the zone-selection rule and weight-class filtering in ZoneRouter, which stay unchanged
block-level weight or dimension fitness, because block.column_count is NULL for all 112 rows and the field survey in docs/block-capability-README.md has not been collected
slot-level or pallet-level destinations, because parking_slot has no generated rows
LED panel frames, PLC and HMI register contracts, and vehicle classification rules
server push such as SignalR or server-sent events; the existing polling pattern is kept
authentication or authorisation for the driver view
regenerating Images/plan_map.jpg or recomputing block.map_x and block.map_y

findings.summary: block.column_count is NULL for all 112 block rows, so v_zone_capacity.total_tier0 and total_ground both sum to zero and ZoneRouter answers NO_CAPACITY for 2600KG and THUONG vehicles today. Only 2200KG reaches a ROUTED decision, so the barrier screen will show the message state for two of three weight classes until the field survey in docs/block-capability-README.md is collected. The feature is correct as specified, but its visible coverage is limited by data this spec deliberately leaves out of scope.

The script that rendered Images/plan_map.jpg from the CAD drawing is not committed; TotalParking/scratch holds no renderer, and 34_block_map_xy.sql records the transform in prose only. The lane network inherits that fragility: if the background image is ever regenerated, neither the block coordinates nor the lane nodes can be reproduced from the repository alone. D2's hand-trace reversal bounds the risk for this feature but does not remove it.

The floor_plan table still holds exactly one row, B1, describing zones_map.jpeg at 1016 by 781, while the routing map frame lives only in the BlockMapRepository constants. Two frame declarations therefore coexist and disagree. I1 keeps this feature on the code-side declaration, but a later reader may reasonably mistake floor_plan for the authority.

The pending-assignment debit is computed inside the ranking read and is not transactional, so two ingest calls arriving together can still observe the same free count and assign the same block. The Data and Consistency section states this residual effect and why a reserving parking_session row is ruled out at camera time; it is an accepted limit rather than an unnoticed defect.

graph_coverage.notes: Each of the 19 acceptance criteria has one counterexample naming concrete values, and each maps to exactly one implementation owner task.
The freshness window D8 is exercised from both the allocation side, through the R2.5 debit, and the display side, through R4.2 and R4.3, so the two consumers of the same window cannot drift apart.

The chain from POST /vehicle through ZoneRouter, the allocator, vehicle_routing, GET /Monitor/DriverRoute and the kiosk view is anchored end to end; every V definition names an existing controller or view entrypoint.

Four repository facts are grounded to exact migrations, views and source files; two reversible assumptions carry bounded reversal boundaries; three user-owned decisions are recorded as resolved by explicit user selection.

Both migrations are information_schema guarded and additive, existing vehicle_routing rows read back with a null block_no, and the rollback path of dropping the lane tables returns the endpoint to its documented 503 behaviour without touching any existing table.

counterexamples.scenario: A lane node digitised from a title-block region of the drawing lands at x equal to 1247, outside the 1200 by 1139 routing frame, and is inserted without complaint; the driver view then draws the path running off the right edge of the plan image.
counterexamples.expected: The migration frame check reports the offending node_id and the migration is not accepted, so no node outside the frame ever reaches the route service.

counterexamples.scenario: A second ramp is digitised later and a second lane node is also flagged is_entry; Dijkstra then starts from whichever row the loader happens to read first, so the same vehicle is shown two different paths across application restarts.
counterexamples.expected: The migration fails and names both node ids, keeping exactly one entry origin so the path start is never decided by row order.

counterexamples.scenario: Block 87 keeps a null lane_node_id because the aisle serving it was never digitised; every vehicle the allocator sends there produces a no-route answer and the barrier screen shows text where a path belongs.
counterexamples.expected: The migration lists block_no 87 among mapped blocks with no arrival node and fails, so the gap surfaces at migration time rather than through a waiting driver.

counterexamples.scenario: An operator re-runs the migration after a partial failure; without idempotent upserts the edge inserts abort on a primary key collision and leave the graph half-loaded, so some zones route and others silently do not.
counterexamples.expected: The second run completes and reports node, edge, and arrival-node totals identical to the first run, making a re-run a safe recovery step.

counterexamples.scenario: The allocator ranks candidates across every zone instead of inside the zone the router chose, so a vehicle routed to zone 5 is assigned a block in zone 1 while the LED arrows still point toward zone 5.
counterexamples.expected: Every persisted ROUTED row names a block whose zone_id equals the decision zone_id, and the check reports zero cross-zone rows.

counterexamples.scenario: Every PLC in the routed zone has been offline for an hour, so each block reports zero taken slots and looks empty; ranked on free count alone the allocator sends the driver to a block that is physically full.
counterexamples.expected: Candidates with a PLC read inside 5 minutes outrank those without, and when all candidates are stale the row is still written with the unverified-occupancy marker set so the surface can say the count is inferred.

counterexamples.scenario: The driver is reading the screen when another vehicle parks in the assigned block; a read path that recomputes the choice swaps the label from block 47 to block 52 mid-glance and the driver follows a path to the wrong place.
counterexamples.expected: Every later read returns the block_no written on the first save, so the destination cannot move while a driver is looking at it.

counterexamples.scenario: A routed zone whose blocks are all at slot_count still yields outcome ROUTED with no block; the endpoint reports a route state with nothing to draw and the barrier screen shows a blank map.
counterexamples.expected: The decision is persisted as NO_CAPACITY with a null block, and the check constraint refuses any ROUTED row carrying a null block_no.

counterexamples.scenario: Two vehicles pass the camera 10 seconds apart when the best candidate has exactly one free space; with no debit both decisions name that block and the second driver arrives to find it occupied.
counterexamples.expected: The second decision names a different block because the first assignment, still inside the display window, is subtracted from that candidate free capacity.

counterexamples.scenario: Two lane paths to the destination have equal total length and the loader returns edges in whatever order the database chooses; consecutive polls alternate between them and the drawn path flickers while the driver watches.
counterexamples.expected: Equal-cost ties resolve on the lower node_id, so repeated calls over an unchanged lane network return the identical point sequence.

counterexamples.scenario: The endpoint returns the path reversed, beginning at the destination block and ending at the ramp; the view draws it faithfully and the animation runs the driver back out of the garage.
counterexamples.expected: The first point holds the entry node coordinates and the last holds the destination arrival node coordinates, expressed in the frame the response reports.

counterexamples.scenario: The lane graph is missing the edge into one aisle, leaving block 61 detached; a straight-line fallback is drawn instead and the line crosses six parked blocks on the way.
counterexamples.expected: The endpoint answers with the message state naming block 61 and an empty route, and the recursive reachability query lists that arrival node so the gap is visible before a driver meets it.

counterexamples.scenario: The kiosk view hardcodes its own overlay dimensions; the plan image is later re-rendered at a different size and every drawn path sits offset from the block it points at, with nothing in the page reporting a mismatch.
counterexamples.expected: The overlay takes its viewBox from the frame the response reports, so the path and the blocks stay in one coordinate system whenever the image is regenerated.

counterexamples.scenario: Two vehicles are decided one second apart; the view renders whichever response arrives first, so the driver at the barrier is shown the destination computed for the car ahead.
counterexamples.expected: The decision with the later decided_at is the one drawn, and it appears within 3 seconds of becoming readable.

counterexamples.scenario: A vehicle drives away and no new event arrives; the previous path stays on the screen and the next driver to stop at the barrier follows a route computed for a different car.
counterexamples.expected: Once the window lapses the view shows its waiting state with no path element and no destination label left in the page.

counterexamples.scenario: An oversize vehicle is rejected and the decision carries no block; the view keeps the previous path drawn beside the rejection text and the driver reads the leftover line as the instruction.
counterexamples.expected: The reason text renders on its own, with no path element and no destination label present.

counterexamples.scenario: The view is created but never added to the project file; it works under F5 during acceptance, Publish silently omits it, and the barrier television shows a 404 in production with nothing in the build reporting a problem.
counterexamples.expected: The view file is listed as a Content Include entry, sets the SCADA layout, and has its action name in the sidebar expression before the task counts as delivered.

counterexamples.scenario: The JavaScript block pick is kept as a fallback for responses without a destination; on a no-data answer the operator map highlights a block the system never chose and an operator relays it as the assigned destination.
counterexamples.expected: The view contains no filter, sort, or pick over the block list and highlights only the block the server named, so the page cannot display a decision that was never made.

counterexamples.scenario: The operator preview is wired through the same save used by the live camera path; every weight-class click writes a routing row, the recent-vehicle list fills with cars that never arrived, and the pending-assignment debit removes capacity for them.
counterexamples.expected: The vehicle_event, vehicle_profile, and vehicle_routing row counts taken either side of a preview call are identical.

reviewer_evidence.summary: Elevated assurance: authoring-side semantic review of the whole graph with one counterexample per acceptance criterion and four recorded non-blocking findings. No independent reviewer attestation is claimed, and no execution proof is claimed.

criteria.text: When the lane-network migration runs, the system shall persist every lane node with coordinates inside the routing map frame, where the frame bounds are `0 <= x <= 1200` and `0 <= y <= 1139` as declared by `BlockMapRepository.ViewW` and `BlockMapRepository.ViewH`, and shall reject the migration when any node falls outside those bounds.
The system shall persist exactly one lane node marked as the ramp entry origin, and shall fail the migration when zero or more than one node carries that mark.

When the migration runs, the system shall attach every `block` row having `map_x IS NOT NULL` to exactly one lane node as that block's arrival node, and shall list the offending `block_no` values and fail when any such block has zero or more than one arrival node.
When the migration is executed a second time against an already-migrated database, the system shall produce the identical node, edge, and arrival-node rows without raising a duplicate-key error.

When `ZoneRouter` returns outcome `ROUTED` for a Camera AI event, the system shall select exactly one block whose `zone_id` equals the routed zone and whose observed occupancy is below its `slot_count`.

When at least one candidate block has a `plc_slot_state` row read within the last 5 minutes, the system shall select only from those blocks; when no candidate has such a row, the system shall still select a block and shall mark the returned decision as unverified occupancy.
When a destination block has been persisted for an event, the system shall return that stored block on every later read of that event and shall not recompute the selection.
If no block in the routed zone has occupancy below its `slot_count`, then the system shall persist outcome `NO_CAPACITY` with a null block and shall not persist outcome `ROUTED`.

When selecting a block, the system shall subtract from each candidate's free count the number of destination blocks already persisted for other events inside the display freshness window, so that two vehicles arriving within that window are not both sent to a block that only has room for one.

When a route to a block is requested, the system shall return a minimum-total-cost node sequence from the ramp origin node to that block's arrival node, where an edge's cost is the Euclidean distance between its endpoints in the routing map frame, and shall return the same sequence on every repeated request while the lane network is unchanged.

The system shall return the route as an ordered array of point objects, each carrying an `x` and a `y` field in the routing map frame, whose first element holds the ramp origin node coordinates and whose last element holds the requested block's arrival node coordinates.

If no sequence of edges connects the ramp origin node to the requested block's arrival node, then the system shall return an explicit no-route result naming the unreachable `block_no`, and shall not return a straight-line, axis-aligned, or partial point array.

When a routing decision with a destination block is current, the driver view shall render the floor-plan image at the routing map frame, the returned route as a single drawn path, and the destination block number as a text label.

When a new routing decision is persisted, the driver view shall display that decision's route within 3 seconds of it becoming readable, and shall display the most recently decided `ROUTED` event when several are inside the freshness window.
When no routing decision falls inside the freshness window, the driver view shall display a waiting state and shall remove any previously drawn path rather than leaving the last route on screen.
When the current decision's outcome is `REJECTED`, `NO_CAPACITY`, `NO_DATA`, or `MANUAL`, the driver view shall display that outcome's reason text and shall draw no path and no destination label.

The driver view file shall be listed as a `<Content Include>` item in `TotalParking/TotalParking.csproj`, shall set `Layout = "~/Views/Shared/_ScadaLayout.cshtml"`, and its action name shall be present in the sidebar active-state expression in `TotalParking/Views/Shared/_ScadaLayout.cshtml`.

The map on `TotalParking/Views/Home/Routing.cshtml` shall render the destination block supplied by the server, and the view shall contain no client-side candidate filtering, sorting, or selection of blocks.

When the operator runs a weight-class simulation, the system shall choose the previewed destination block through the same server-side selection used for real Camera AI events, and shall write no `vehicle_event`, `vehicle_profile`, or `vehicle_routing` row while doing so.

design_records.title: Driver route endpoint response contract
design_records.text: - **Owner:** the route service and endpoint task. - **Consumers:** the driver guidance view, the operator page. - **Shape/behaviour:** - **Method and route:** `GET /Monitor/DriverRoute`, no parameters. - **Auth:** none, consistent with every other action on the monitor controller. - **Required headers:** none. The response carries `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. - **Success response, 200:** a JSON object whose fields are `now`, `view_w`, `view_h`, `state`, `event_id`, `outcome`, `reason`, `zone_id`, `block_no`, `occupancy_verified`, and `route`. `state` is exactly one of `ROUTE`, `MESSAGE`, or `WAITING`. `ROUTE` requires a non-null `block_no` and a `route` array of at least two point objects, each carrying an `x` and a `y` field. `MESSAGE` carries `outcome` and `reason` with a null `block_no` and an empty `route`. `WAITING` carries a null `event_id`, a null `outcome`, a null `block_no`, and an empty `route`. - **Error semantics:** `503` carrying a single `error` field when the lane or routing views are unavailable, matching the existing behaviour of the routing state endpoint; `500` carrying the same single `error` field on any other failure. No 4xx exists because the endpoint takes no input. - **Idempotency and concurrency:** read-only. Two calls inside the same decision's D8 window return the same `event_id`, `block_no`, and `route`. The endpoint writes no row and touches no PLC. - **Compatibility:** additive. The block map and routing state endpoints keep their current shapes; the simulate endpoint gains `block_no` and `route`.

design_records.title: vehicle_routing destination block column
design_records.text: - **Owner:** the block allocation task. - **Consumers:** the route endpoint, the operator page. - **Shape/behaviour:** `vehicle_routing` gains `block_no SMALLINT UNSIGNED NULL` with a foreign key to `block (block_no)`. It is non-null only when `outcome = 'ROUTED'`, enforced by a check constraint. `outcome` keeps the five values established by `11_remove_demo_data.sql`: `ROUTED`, `NO_CAPACITY`, `NO_DATA`, `REJECTED`, `MANUAL`. - **Compatibility:** existing rows keep a null `block_no`, so historical decisions read back as decisions without a destination rather than as errors. The column is added by a re-runnable `ALTER` guarded on `information_schema`, the pattern already used by `34_block_map_xy.sql`.

design_records.title: Lane network schema
design_records.text: - **Owner:** the lane network migration task. - **Consumers:** the route service. - **Shape/behaviour:** `lane_node (node_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED PRIMARY KEY, x SMALLINT NOT NULL, y SMALLINT NOT NULL, is_entry TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)` and `lane_edge (from_node, to_node, PRIMARY KEY (from_node, to_node))` with both endpoints foreign-keyed to `lane_node`. Edges are undirected and stored once per unordered pair; the route service expands each row in both directions. `block` gains `lane_node_id SMALLINT UNSIGNED NULL` foreign-keyed to `lane_node`, which is that block's arrival node. Edge cost is not stored; it is computed from the endpoint coordinates so that moving a node cannot leave a stale cost behind. - **Compatibility:** two new tables and one new nullable column. No existing table, view, or column changes shape.

design_records.title: One routing map frame, declared once
design_records.text: - **Decision:** All lane node coordinates, all block arrival coordinates, and both views use the frame already declared by `BlockMapRepository.ViewW = 1200` and `BlockMapRepository.ViewH = 1139`, which is the pixel frame of `TotalParking/Images/plan_map.jpg`. The lane tables store plain integer `x` and `y` in that frame and carry no separate scale, offset, or `floor_plan_id`. - **Rejects ambiguity:** Do not attach the lane network to the `floor_plan` row `B1`. That row still describes `~/Images/zones_map.jpeg` at 1016 by 781, a different image at a different scale, and `block.map_x` and `block.map_y` do not live in it. Do not restate `1200` or `1139` as a literal in the new service or in either view. - **Negative path:** The migration fails and names each offending row when any node lies outside `0 <= x <= 1200` or `0 <= y <= 1139`. - **Anchors:** A-D-01, A-D-03, A-D-09, A-D-10

design_records.title: The driver view polls; nothing is pushed
design_records.text: - **Decision:** The driver view polls the route endpoint every 2 seconds, which satisfies the 3-second display budget of R4.2 without a push channel. - **Rejects ambiguity:** Do not add SignalR, WebSockets, or server-sent events. The solution targets .NET Framework 4.5 and every existing live surface in the project refreshes by polling. - **Negative path:** A failed poll leaves the last rendered state untouched until the next poll succeeds or the decision leaves the D8 window, whichever happens first. - **Anchors:** A-D-01

design_records.title: Lane geometry comes from the same drawing and the same transform as the block coordinates
design_records.text: - **Decision:** Aisle centre lines are taken from page 1 of the mechanical parking system drawing and mapped into the routing frame with the transform already recorded in `34_block_map_xy.sql`: `point_pdf = raw * 0.06`, `pixel = point_pdf * 2.0`, `pixel_y = page_height_pt - point_pdf_y`. Using the same source and the same transform as `block.map_x` and `block.map_y` is what keeps lane nodes and block dots in one frame. - **Rejects ambiguity:** Do not fit lane geometry to the rendered image by colour detection, bounding-box matching, or per-zone alignment. `34_block_map_xy.sql` records four such attempts failing at 68 percent, 79 percent, and a 15.6 percent axis-ratio error, for the stated reason that the older image had no shared anchor with the drawing. - **Negative path:** If aisle linework cannot be isolated from that content stream, the bounded reversal is to hand-trace the lane centre lines against `plan_map.jpg` and insert the same node and edge rows. The stored schema, the frame, and every consumer are unchanged by that reversal, so it stays inside the migration file. - **Anchors:** A-D-09, A-D-10, A-D-11

design_records.title: The ramp head becomes a data node, not a code constant
design_records.text: - **Decision:** The ramp entry point is one lane node flagged `is_entry = 1`. The route service resolves the path origin by reading that flagged node. - **Rejects ambiguity:** Do not compute a route from `BlockMapRepository.GateX` and `GateY` and then snap to the nearest lane node at request time. The snap result would move silently whenever the lane network is edited, and `BlockMapRepository.cs` already records that those two constants were placed by hand because the drawing carries no ramp label. - **Negative path:** The migration fails when the count of nodes with `is_entry = 1` is not exactly one. - **Anchors:** A-D-01, A-D-11

design_records.title: Shortest path is Dijkstra over Euclidean edge cost, with no geometric fallback
design_records.text: - **Decision:** Route cost is the sum of Euclidean distances between edge endpoints in the routing frame. When the origin and the target arrival node are disconnected, the service returns an explicit no-route result naming the `block_no`. - **Rejects ambiguity:** Do not fall back to the two-segment gate-to-target polyline the operator page draws today, and do not return the partial path explored so far. On a driver-facing screen a line that crosses through blocks is an instruction to drive through them. - **Negative path:** A disconnected target yields no route; the caller renders outcome text and draws nothing. - **Anchors:** A-D-01, A-D-10

design_records.title: Block choice is made on observed occupancy only
design_records.text: - **Decision:** Within the zone `ZoneRouter` already chose, the destination block is the candidate with the greatest free capacity, where free capacity is `block.slot_count` minus that block's rows in `v_slot_taken` minus the pending-assignment debit of D9. Ties break on the lower `block_no` so the result is deterministic. - **Rejects ambiguity:** Do not filter candidate blocks by weight class, length, or pallet rating. `block.column_count` is `NULL` for all 112 rows, so `v_zone_capacity.total_tier0` sums to zero and any block-level weight rule would be computed from absent data. `docs/block-capability-README.md` states that this field survey has not been collected and that block choice cannot be deployed without it. Weight-class filtering stays where it already is, at zone level. - **Negative path:** When no candidate has free capacity above zero, the decision is `NO_CAPACITY` with a null block, never `ROUTED` without a block. - **Anchors:** A-D-02, A-D-07, A-D-12

design_records.title: A block the PLC has not reported recently is ranked last and labelled
design_records.text: - **Decision:** Candidates with a `plc_slot_state` row whose `read_at` is within the last 5 minutes are preferred over candidates without one. When only stale candidates remain, one is still chosen and the decision is marked as unverified occupancy so every surface can say so. - **Rejects ambiguity:** Do not treat a block with no recent PLC read as empty and rank it first on that basis; its occupancy is an inference, and `BlockMapRepository.cs` already exposes `fresh` for exactly this distinction. Equally, do not exclude stale blocks entirely, because during commissioning that would leave a whole zone with no destination. - **Negative path:** All candidates stale means the chosen block is returned with the unverified marker set, not suppressed. - **Anchors:** A-D-01, A-D-06

design_records.title: A persisted destination block is final for that event
design_records.text: - **Decision:** The destination block is computed once, when the routing decision is made for an event, and written in the same save as the outcome. Every later read returns the stored value. - **Rejects ambiguity:** Do not recompute the block on each poll of the driver view or the operator page. The driver view polls while a driver is looking at it, so a recomputed choice would move the destination mid-glance as other vehicles park. - **Negative path:** A read for an event with no persisted block returns that event's outcome without a block, never a freshly computed one. - **Anchors:** A-D-04

design_records.title: Display freshness window for a routing decision
design_records.text: - **Decision:** A routing decision is shown on the driver view only while it is inside a 90-second window. - **Clock anchor:** `vehicle_routing.decided_at`, the moment the destination became valid. - **Clock source:** MySQL `NOW(3)` evaluated in the same connection that reads the row, on the same host that runs both the ingest endpoint and the site. - **Timezone and precision:** server local time with no UTC conversion, matching every `DateTime.Now` already used across the controllers; the column is `DATETIME(3)` and the comparison is made at millisecond precision. - **Comparator and inclusivity:** the decision is current while `NOW(3) - decided_at <= 90 seconds`, inclusive at exactly 90 seconds and excluded beyond it. - **Enforcement boundary:** the server, inside the route endpoint's query. The browser never decides freshness and never filters by time. - **Rejects ambiguity:** Do not anchor the window on `vehicle_event.camera_timestamp` or on `vehicle_event.received_at`. - **Wrong-clock counterexample:** `camera_timestamp` is nullable, because the ingest layer normalises the camera's `0` and `"Unknown"` to `null`; a null anchor makes such a decision either permanently current or permanently stale depending on how the null is coerced, and neither is the truth. `received_at` fails differently: the ingest layer documents that the app pool recycles at 03:00 with the old and new workers both alive for up to 90 seconds, so a queued burst can be decided minutes after it was received. A decision made one second ago would then be suppressed as stale and the driver waiting at the barrier would see the idle screen. - **Boundary counterexample:** a decision aged exactly 90.000 seconds is still shown; at 90.001 seconds the view returns to the waiting state. - **Anchors:** A-D-04

design_records.title: Assignments already handed out are debited before the next choice
design_records.text: - **Decision:** When choosing a block, each candidate's free capacity is reduced by the number of destination blocks already persisted for other events whose `decided_at` is inside the D8 window and whose vehicle has not yet been observed parked. - **Rejects ambiguity:** Do not create a `parking_session` row to reserve the destination. `08_vehicle_routing.sql` records why: a session belongs to an RFID card, a camera event has no card, and a session created here would be duplicated when the driver later scans at the HMI, with no column able to join the two. - **Negative path:** Two vehicles detected 10 seconds apart when the best block has exactly one free space: the first is sent there, the second sees that block debited to zero and is sent to the next candidate. - **Anchors:** A-D-04, A-D-07

design_records.title: The routing map frame is declared exactly once in code
design_records.text: `BlockMapRepository.ViewW` and `BlockMapRepository.ViewH` remain the only code-side declaration of the routing frame. The lane service, the route endpoint, the driver view, and the operator view all take their `viewBox` from values served by the API instead of restating those numbers as their own literals.

design_records.title: No routing or selection rule exists in browser JavaScript
design_records.text: Zone choice, block choice, freshness, and path geometry are all decided server-side. Browser code draws only what the server sent. A block-candidate filter, sort, or pick written in JavaScript violates this invariant.

design_records.title: A path is drawn only when a stored block and a computed route both exist
design_records.text: A path is drawn only when the response carries both a persisted destination `block_no` and a route array of at least two points. Every other response state renders text only.

design_records.title: A new SCADA view is not delivered until it is registered
design_records.text: A view added under `Views/Home` counts as delivered only when its file is listed as a `<Content Include>` entry in `TotalParking/TotalParking.csproj`, it sets `Layout = "~/Views/Shared/_ScadaLayout.cshtml"`, and its action name appears in the sidebar active-state expression. Razor compiles views at runtime, so an unregistered view still serves under F5 while Publish silently omits it; ten existing views are already missing from the project file for this reason.

verification_definitions.expected: every result row reports PASS, the count of nodes outside the frame bounds is 0, the count of is_entry nodes is exactly 1, the count of blocks with a non-null map_x and no arrival node is 0, and a second run of the migration reports the same node and edge totals
verification_definitions.negative: inserting a node at x equal to 1300 or a second is_entry node makes the matching result row report FAIL and print the offending node_id

verification_definitions.expected: every ROUTED row carries a non-null block_no whose zone_id equals the row zone_id, every non-ROUTED row carries a null block_no, no ROUTED row points at a block whose v_slot_taken count already equals its slot_count, a candidate with a plc_slot_state read inside 5 minutes outranks one without, and re-reading an event returns the block_no written on its first save
verification_definitions.negative: inserting a ROUTED row with a null block_no, or a NO_CAPACITY row with a non-null block_no, is refused by the check constraint and the script records that refusal as PASS

verification_definitions.expected: the recursive reachability query lists zero unreachable arrival nodes, the returned route begins at the is_entry node and ends at the destination block arrival node, and the two calls return identical route arrays
verification_definitions.negative: a block whose arrival node has no edge path is listed by the query as unreachable and the endpoint returns state MESSAGE naming that block_no with an empty route instead of any point array

verification_definitions.expected: the seeded row aged 89 seconds resolves to state ROUTE, the row aged 91 seconds resolves to state WAITING, a seeded NO_CAPACITY row inside the window resolves to state MESSAGE, the opened page renders the plan image with one drawn path and the destination block number, and the view path appears as a Content Include entry in the project file with its action name in the sidebar expression
verification_definitions.negative: a seeded row whose outcome is REJECTED renders its reason text with no drawn path and no destination label, and the previously drawn path is cleared when the window lapses instead of being left on screen

verification_definitions.expected: the simulate response carries a server-selected block_no, the operator map draws that block, and the view file contains no filter, sort, or pick over the block list in JavaScript
verification_definitions.negative: the vehicle_event, vehicle_profile, and vehicle_routing row counts recorded before and after the simulate call differ by zero, and any non-zero difference fails the check

decisions.statement: The routing map frame is 1200 by 1139, declared by BlockMapRepository.ViewW and ViewH and matching the viewBox already used by the Routing.cshtml map overlay; block.map_x and block.map_y are exact in that frame.
decisions.evidence: TotalParking/Services/BlockMapRepository.cs declares ViewW 1200 and ViewH 1139; TotalParking/Views/Home/Routing.cshtml uses viewBox 0 0 1200 1139; TotalParking/Database/34_block_map_xy.sql records the transform and states the coordinates are exact rather than fitted.

decisions.statement: The floor_plan table is not the frame authority for the routing map: its only row B1 still points at ~/Images/zones_map.jpeg at 1016 by 781, a different image at a different scale from plan_map.jpg.
decisions.evidence: TotalParking/Database/05_parking_topology.sql inserts floor_plan code B1 with image_path ~/Images/zones_map.jpeg, width_units 1016 and height_units 781.

decisions.statement: Block-level weight fitness cannot be computed today: block.column_count is NULL for every block row, so v_zone_capacity.total_tier0 sums to zero and 2600KG and THUONG vehicles currently route to NO_CAPACITY for a data reason rather than a parking reason.
decisions.evidence: TotalParking/Database/dump_20260919.sql block rows carry NULL column_count; TotalParking/Database/07_parking_session.sql defines total_tier0 as SUM(column_count) for Mechanical blocks; docs/block-capability-README.md states the field survey behind these columns has not been collected.

decisions.statement: The destination block shown on the operator map today is chosen in browser JavaScript and is never persisted, so the map can show a block the server never decided.
decisions.evidence: TotalParking/Views/Home/Routing.cshtml filters map.blocks by zone and free space, sorts on online and free count, and picks cand[0]; TotalParking/Database/08_vehicle_routing.sql stores zone_id only and has no block column.

decisions.statement: Lane centre lines are extracted from page 1 of the mechanical parking system drawing using the same transform that produced block.map_x and block.map_y, rather than being traced by hand.
decisions.evidence: Bounded reversal: if the aisle linework cannot be isolated from that content stream, hand-trace the centre lines against plan_map.jpg and insert the same lane_node and lane_edge rows. The C3 schema, the routing frame, and every consumer are unchanged, so the reversal is confined to TotalParking/Database/37_lane_network.sql.

decisions.statement: The display freshness window is 90 seconds, long enough for a driver to stop at the barrier and read the screen and short enough that a departed vehicle's route is not left showing.
decisions.evidence: Bounded reversal: the window is one comparator in the DriverRoute query defined by D8; changing the number changes no schema, no contract field, and no consumer. It is revisited if commissioning shows drivers arriving at the block before or after the path clears.

decisions.statement: The barrier screen is a new full-screen kiosk view rather than a reuse of the operator Dieu huong xe page.
decisions.evidence: User selected a new kiosk/TV page, keeping Routing.cshtml as the operator console with its simulation buttons, zone density, and device-status panels.

decisions.statement: The drawn path follows a real lane graph searched with Dijkstra rather than the existing schematic two-segment polyline.
decisions.evidence: User selected the real lane graph option, accepting the lane-network digitisation work that ZoneRouter.cs notes had not been surveyed.

decisions.statement: The server selects the destination block and persists it with the routing decision, rather than suggesting one per request or routing only to a zone.
decisions.evidence: User selected server-chosen and persisted block, accepting the vehicle_routing contract change and the removal of the JavaScript block selection.
